sys_atf_test.description: POST /api/x_casemgmt/case_submit with Content-Type application/json must answer HTTP 201 carrying the generated case number and the verbatim message "Your case has been submitted", and the created case must land with status Draft and a CASE0000001-format number. Steps 2-8 assert that contract through the ATF-instrumented Send REST Request - Inbound step, which carries no credentials: the platform serves it as guest, its response carries X-Is-Logged-In false and the row it creates is guest-owned, so the 201 contract is asserted on behalf of a genuinely unauthenticated caller - and because ATF instruments that step type the insert sits inside the rollback context, measured on 2026-08-08 when a run whose step 10 had been skipped still came back clean. That step type cannot vary its request, so step 9 covers the rest of the anonymous surface from a server-side script with no credentials, WITHOUT persisting anything: an unauthenticated POST whose payload the handler must reject comes back carrying the handler own verbatim validation message, which a 401 or 403 from the authenticator could never do; the case step 2 submitted is read back through the anonymous lookup endpoint and exposes only status, subject and opened_date; and a census proves neither of those calls persisted a case. An earlier design submitted a valid case from that script - an outbound call from a script is NOT ATF-instrumented, so the rollback reversed this test own cleanup delete and every run left one synthetic case behind. It no longer does: this test asserts its own cleanliness.
